I'll start by looking at the project layout and the build contract.

That call was malformed. I'll write the makefile fragments with `write_file`.

The shell call was empty again. I'll retry with a concrete command.

Now the code fixes. Next I'll build to see which warnings the compiler reports, to compare with what I found by reading.

Matches my reading. Now the source fixes.

The project now builds and meets `docs/BUILDING.md`. I checked this on clean trees at `-j8`, and `/app/STATUS.json` says `success`.

**What I ran**
- Each target (`all`, `build/lib/libqs.a`, `build/bin/colstat`, `build/bin/qcalc`, `check`, `install`) built from a clean tree at `-j8`, three times each, with no failures.
- `make check` passed: 22 unit tests and 34 golden cases. It also passed under `make DEBUG=1 check`.
- A second `make` with nothing changed ran no compile, archive or link step.
- Changing `VERSION`, a header, or `src/ops.def` rebuilt the dependent objects and the programs.
- `make install` with `PREFIX='/opt/my&pre|fix'` and a `DESTDIR` installed exactly the files and modes the contract lists, and `qs.pc` recorded that prefix. A program built against the installed header and `libqs.a` with `-lm` built and ran.

**Makefile fixes**
- The programs didn't depend on `libqs.a`, and the link line put libraries before the objects. I fixed both.
- `version.h` was never generated. It is now built from `VERSION` with `build-aux/mkversion.sh`.
- There was no header dependency tracking, so I added it. Generated headers are produced before any compile.
- `DEBUG=1` was never recognised, because the makefile tested for `yes`. A stamp file now rebuilds everything when the flags or `CC` change. It also covers a switch from release to debug on an existing `build/`.
- `check` ignored unit-test failures and lost the golden suite's exit status through `tee`. It now runs both suites and fails if either fails.
- `install` didn't install `qcalc.1`, and `qs.pc` was built at make time with whatever `PREFIX` was set then. It is now written during `install` with the given `PREFIX`.
- `all` also built `qs.pc`, which isn't part of the contract, so I removed that.
- I deleted the stale hand-written `include/qs/ops.h`. It disagreed with `ops.def`: wrong `neg` precedence, `pow` left-associative, and no `hypot` or `clamp`.

**Code fixes (all warnings fixed in the code, with no pragmas or `-Wno-` flags)**
- Fixed unused parameters and variables, sign-compare, `%d` used with `size_t`, a missing `<stdlib.h>`, an assignment used as a condition, an unhandled `TOK_END` case, and switch fallthrough.
- Prefix `-` now takes as its operand only the operators that bind strictly tighter than `neg`, as `docs/qcalc.md` says. This gives the same results for the current `ops.def`.
- `--max-size` could overflow silently, for example `16777216g` wrapped to 0. A size too large for `size_t` now saturates, since no input can exceed it. I read the docs as meaning that rather than a usage error, but they don't say.

With no `-c`, `colstat` reports every header column by position. For a duplicated header name, the later column gets its own statistics rather than the first occurrence's. `docs/colstat.md` is ambiguous here and no golden case covers it, so I left that behaviour alone.

I left `build/` removed (`make clean`).
